nodes.question: Why are transboundary fish stocks considered to be at risk of overexploitation?
nodes.answer: Transboundary fish stocks are at risk of overexploitation because fishing nations tend to respond to individual non-cooperative incentives, leading to overly aggressive behavior and over-extraction.
nodes.paragraph: 2023). Yet practical challenges exist for marine reserves to be successfully implemented. Many species move over large distances as adults or lar - vae, which can be at odds with the spatial boundaries of a reserve (Cowen and Sponaugle 2009 ; Song et al. 2017 ). Furthermore, reserves that produce measurable outcomes require sustainable financing to support staffing and enforce- ment, which can be challenging for low-capacity countries (Grorud-Colvert et al. 2021; Millage et al. 2021). nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What predicts a high-value BMRA in the context of adult movement?
nodes.answer: High adult movement, particularly when the movement to the fishing patch outweighs the movement to the reserve patch by 10-30%, predicts a high-value BMRA.
nodes.paragraph: We dis- cuss the challenges of the practical application of BMRA using four real-world transboundary stocks. We find that high adult movement predicts a high-value BMRA, in par - ticular when adult movement to the fishing patch outweighs adult movement to the reserve patch by 10 30%. Further - more, we find that BMRA is most likely to be agreed for transboundary stocks with high adult movement, although larval dispersal can bolster agreement acceptance and increase the agreement negotiation space if adult movement is low. Lastly, we compare the gains under BMRA to the gains under a fully cooperative fishing agreement where both countries continue to harvest. We find that BMRA can repro- duce these fully cooperative gains if adult movement from the fishing patch to the reserve patch is low ( 40%), and adult movement from the reserve patch to the fishing patch is high ( 60%), regardless of larval movement. In some cases, the BMRA conservation gains exceeded the fully coopera- tive outcome under certain spatial connectivity conditions; however, economic gains were always equal or lower. Incomplete ownership of a resource can reduce the effec- tiveness of marine reserves, and this poses a particular chal- lenge for transboundary stocks where adults move or larvae disperse over large distances (White and Costello 2011).

nodes.question: What are some countries with the lowest mean annual fishing biocapacity?
nodes.answer: Central African Republic, Lesotho, South Sudan, Afghanistan, Serbia & Montenegro, Luxembourg, Niger, Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Iraq are some countries with the lowest mean annual fishing biocapacity.
